selected_evidence.requirement: Sudo commands are recorded with user and timestamp in /var/log/sudo-commands.log
selected_evidence.summary: Log file shows entries like 'Aug 26 10:39:46 node1 sudo: antrieb : TTY=unknown ; PWD=... ; USER=root ; COMMAND=/bin/whoami' confirming timestamp, user, and command are captured

selected_evidence.requirement: Sudo command entries are kept out of the general system log (/var/log/messages)
selected_evidence.summary: grep for COMMAND= in /var/log/messages shows only pre-config-change entries; commands issued after rsyslog restart (whoami, id, cat) do not appear there
Captured boot_id 16724682-15d4-4e48-bfb9-a2913f22f416, confirmed rsyslog active, and sudo-commands.log had 14 healthy entries prior to restart

selected_evidence.requirement: Node restart proven via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Node was unreachable mid-reboot (connection timeout), then came back with a new boot_id 8a973a0c-8c80-4de9-8dee-057f318601fd, differing from the baseline 16724682-...

selected_evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of sudo logging and exclusion from general log
selected_evidence.summary: After restart, rsyslog is active, new sudo command (whoami) logged with timestamp/user to /var/log/sudo-commands.log, and /var/log/messages still shows no new COMMAND= entries, confirming the config persisted across reboot
